extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: PURPOSE

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: This policy establishes what a provider should do if they are unsure whether an item or

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: service is covered by Devoted and advises not to use ABNs and GY modifiers for this scenario.

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted covers services consistent with the benefit guidelines in our EOCs and Medicare

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: guidelines. If a provider is unsure if an item or service is covered by Devoted based on the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: EOC, a provider should request a pre-service organization determination before services are

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: rendered or items are obtained.3 Per CMS guidelines, ABNs should not be used for items or

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: services provided by MA plans, where providers have the opportunity to file a pre-service

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: organization determination.1

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted processes claims based on our determination of covered benefits and not on the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: presence or absence of a GY modifier. For this reason, providers do not need to include a GY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: modifier on claims submitted to Devoted. Specifically, Devoted will process claims as follows:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● If the provider does not file a pre-service organization determination and the service or

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: item is not covered, Devoted denies the claim and the provider must assume financial

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: responsibility.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● If the provider does file a pre-service organization determination and Devoted

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: determines the service or item is not covered, Devoted issues a denial notice to the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: member and the provider.4 The member has the right to appeal this decision or to

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: proceed with services knowing the request for coverage was denied. If the member

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: proceeds with services, they are responsible for payment.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● If the provider does file a pre-service organization determination and Devoted

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: determines services are covered, Devoted proceeds with paying the claim.

extracted_content.content: POLICY STATEMENT

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Coverage & Payment Rationale

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health uses CMS national coverage determinations and applicable mandatory local

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: coverage determinations where possible. Devoted Health also uses InterQual® criteria as a

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: clinical-evidence tool to help guide level-of-care and payment determinations. InterQual® is applied

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: in conjunction with physician review of all relevant clinical information to make medical-necessity

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: determinations.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: All determinations for acute admission coverages are made in accordance with Medicare coverage

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: standards, including the Two-Midnight Benchmark (42 CFR § 412.3) and Devoted Health's obligation

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: under 42 CFR § 422.101(c) to follow original Medicare coverage criteria.1, 2, 3

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Acute Admission Criteria & Documentation Requirements

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Baseline Criteria

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Clinical documentation supporting acute admission payment must demonstrate all of the following4:

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Severity of illness and intensity of services that cannot be safely managed in an outpatient or

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: observation setting.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Predictability of adverse events or risk of clinical deterioration.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Need for diagnostic or therapeutic interventions requiring hospital admission.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Relevant co-morbidities or medical history that increase risk or complexity.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ● Admitting physician's reasonable expectation that the hospital care will cross at least two

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: midnights, as documented in the medical record, unless documentation supports a

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: case-by-case exception.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health may request additional documentation (e.g., progress notes, imaging reports, labs,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: ED records, etc.) when the initial submission is incomplete or ambiguous as to whether the clinical

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: severity meets these requirements.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Concurrent and Retrospective Review

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: All acute admissions are subject to concurrent review against the criteria above. If the review results

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: in the determination that documentation does not support inpatient- or observation-level care,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: payment may be appropriately classified to a lower payment rate.5

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Lower Severity Level of Care

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Lower severity-level services are appropriate for conditions requiring short-term monitoring,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: reassessment, or treatment expected to resolve within a limited timeframe.6

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Examples include (but are not limited to): abdominal pain, allergic reaction, altered mental status,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: anemia, asthma, atrial fibrillation, back pain, bronchitis/bronchiolitis, cellulitis, chest pain, COPD,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: croup, dehydration, diabetes mellitus, epistaxis, febrile illness, gastroenteritis, heart failure,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: hemoptysis, migraine, pneumonia, poisoning/toxic ingestion, renal colic, seizures, syncope/collapse,

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: TIA, urinary tract infection, vaginal bleeding (non-obstetrical), and weakness.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: If after 48 hours the patient's condition has not improved sufficiently for discharge, the facility must

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: submit updated clinical documentation supporting conversion to inpatient care.7

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Conversion / Reclassification Requests

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Hospitals may request conversion of a lower-acuity stay payment to higher-acuity inpatient payment

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: when new documentation supports higher-acuity inpatient-level of care.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Requests must be accompanied with additional clinical documentation and reviews will follow a

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: process consistent with Medicare standards and this policy (see Section 3 above).

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Exceptions & Inpatient-Only Procedures

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: This policy does not supersede applicable CMS regulations or contractual terms.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Inpatient payment applies as directed by CMS, including for procedures listed on CMS Addendum E

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: (Inpatient-Only Procedures List), published annually under the Hospital Outpatient Prospective

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Payment System (OPPS) Final Rule in accordance with 42 CFR § 419.22(n), and for other

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: circumstances defined in federal regulation.

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines Devoted Health's payment guidelines for services rendered in a home setting

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: that are billed as inpatient hospital services under the Hospital-at-Home (H@H model). This policy

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: applies to services billed with Revenue Code 0161 and/or Occurrence Span Code 82.

extracted_content.title: SCOPE

extracted_content.content: Applies to all Devoted Health Plans. Exception: Florida Medicaid dual-eligible members in D-SNP

extracted_content.title: SCOPE

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Hospital-at-Home (H@H): A temporary care delivery model authorized under CMS's Acute Hospital

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Care at Home initiative, allowing qualified hospitals to provide inpatient-level services in a

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: beneficiary's home under Section 1135 waiver authority.1

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: CMS established the Hospital at Home Waiver as a voluntary program that allows inpatient-level

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: care to be delivered in the home, and Medicare Advantage plans may choose whether to

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: participate. Devoted Health has elected not to participate in this waiver program and, as a result,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: does not reimburse for inpatient hospital services delivered in the home under the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Hospital-at-Home model.1˒2 Therefore, institutional claims that include Revenue Code 0161,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Occurrence Span Code 82, or otherwise indicate acute inpatient services provided in the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: member's home will not be reimbursed under this payment policy. This policy applies to both

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: in-network and out-of-network providers.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Florida Medicaid dual-eligible members in D-SNP plans are excluded from this policy.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: If a claim includes Hospital-at-Home lines, the entire claim will be denied. Providers must submit a

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: corrected claim, using claim frequency code 7 (replacement claim). Corrected claims must remove all

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Hospital-at-Home lines and reflect only services actually rendered at the inpatient facility.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Providers should not bill inpatient days for care delivered in the home, as:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● The member did not receive facility-based inpatient care

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● Devoted does not reimburse inpatient rates for home-based care

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Once the corrected claim is submitted, the remaining eligible inpatient services will be adjudicated

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: under standard inpatient payment rules.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: If you believe your claim was denied incorrectly and would like us to reconsider, please follow

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: our Provider Dispute process outlined in your provider manual.

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: Ambulatory Surgical Centers (ASCs) are designated facilities that specialize in outpatient

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: procedures that do not require admission to a hospital. Procedures that can be performed in

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: an ASC are statutorily defined by CMS and reviewed each year for potential additions and/or

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: deletions. The purpose of this policy is to establish how we cover and pay for these services.

extracted_content.content: ● Implanted prosthetics, including intra-ocular lenses (IOLs), and related accessories

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Nursing, technicians, and their related services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Radiological services that are not considered separately payable

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Supervision of an anesthetist by the operating surgeon

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Supplies and equipment for the administration and monitoring of anesthesia

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Supplies and other items required to perform the surgery (e.g., surgical dressings,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: splints, casts, equipment)

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: surgery:

extracted_content.content: ● Brachytherapy sources

extracted_content.content: Payment System (OPPS)

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Cost share protections for dual-eligible members

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health members who have limited income and resources may receive help paying

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: out-of-pocket medical expenses from Medicaid. If a member is identified as having additional

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: or secondary insurance coverage through Medicaid (Full Dual (FBDE, SLMB+, QMB+) or QMB),

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the provider should obtain a copy of the member's Medicaid card to bill Medicaid after

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: receiving the Remittance Advice from Devoted Health. No cost shares (copayments,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: coinsurance, or deductibles) should be collected or billed at the time of the visit from a

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: member with Medicaid coverage.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Providers can check members' Medicaid levels via our eligibility check function in Availity.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Additionally, Devoted Health uses remittance advice remark codes (RARCs) to indicate when a

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: member receives cost share assistance (e.g., "Alert: Patient is a Medicaid/Qualified Medicare

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Beneficiary. Review your records for any wrongfully collected deductible. This amount may be

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: billed to a subsequent payer."). When receiving an electronic remittance advice (ERA) that

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: includes such a RARC, providers must follow these instructions and ensure members are not

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: inappropriately billed.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: With respect to any members who are eligible for both Medicare and Medicaid, such members

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: must not be held liable for Medicare Part A and Medicare Part B cost sharing when the State is

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: responsible for paying such amounts. Further, with respect to such members, providers must

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: either (a) accept the payment amount from Devoted Health as payment in full, or (b) bill the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: appropriate State source. The payment by Devoted Health and the payment, if any, by the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: applicable state Medicaid payer shall constitute payment in full for all Medicare services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: rendered to such dual eligible members.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Providers should have a timely process to refund members any difference between the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: copayment collected and the allowable amount for the office visit (when the allowable

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: amount is less than the copay) after the claim is processed by Devoted Health. For assistance

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: with these questions, please contact Devoted Health Provider Services.

extracted_content.content: Devoted Health covering cost share on behalf of Medicaid

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: In Alabama and Florida, for FBDE, SLMB+, QMB+, and QMB members enrolled in D-SNP plans,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: as well as for SLMB+, QMB+, and QMB members in Texas, Devoted Health covers the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: cost-sharing for Medicare services on behalf of Medicaid.6 Providers must accept the payment

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: amount from Devoted Health as payment in full for Medicare services covered under the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: member's Devoted Health plan, and must not seek additional payment from Medicaid or the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: member. For these members, providers should not submit duplicate claims to Medicaid for

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Medicare cost share.

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: with an in-network PCP, they will be assigned to

extracted_content.content: assign or unassign the member based on

extracted_content.content: historical claims data.

extracted_content.content: • If a member has had no encounters with their

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW

extracted_content.content: will be unassigned from that PCP.

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: The purpose of this policy is to establish how Devoted covers and pays for services related to

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: each type of clinical study. Devoted members may participate in Clinical Trials, Investigational

extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Consistent with CMS guidelines, Devoted covers services for members as follows:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Clinical Trials: for clinical trials covered under the Clinical Trials National Coverage

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Determination, Original Medicare pays for routine services for qualifying clinical trials.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted pays the enrollee the difference between original Medicare cost-sharing

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: incurred for qualifying items and services and Devoted's in-network cost-sharing for

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the same category of items and services.1

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● IDE Studies: for CMS-approved Category A and B IDE studies2 covered by local

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Medicare contractors, Devoted pays for routine care items and services and also for

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Category B devices. Devoted will NOT approve Category A devices, which are

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: statutorily excluded from coverage.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● CED Studies: for CMS-approved CED studies3, Devoted pays for items and services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: unless CMS determines the significant cost threshold is exceeded for that item or

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: service.1,4

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Claims for clinical trial services are payable according to fee-for-service rules, with the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: exception that members are not responsible for Part A or B deductibles. Members are,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: however, liable for coinsurance amounts as applicable under Medicare FFS rules.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: For professional claims, please submit on either paper form CMS-1500 or electronic 837P. For

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: institutional claims, please submit on form UB-04 or electronic 837I. Covered outpatient

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: Healthcare Common Procedure Coding System (HCPCS)/Current Procedural Terminology

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: (CPT©) modifiers are two-digit codes added to procedure codes to enhance the clarity and

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: specificity of medical billing by providing additional details about the services or procedures

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: performed. Modifiers adjust reimbursement rates, specify whether only certain components

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: of a procedure were billed, and report multiple or special circumstances. The purpose of this

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: policy is to establish clear guidelines on the application of common modifiers, including when

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: and how to use them when submitting claims.

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted requires the correct use of CPT© and HCPCS modifiers in accordance with CMS

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: guidelines. When a claim includes a modifier, it will be reviewed to ensure the combination of

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the procedure code and modifier is accurate and that the modifier is necessary. Incorrect use

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: of modifiers or claims that require modifiers are submitted without such will result in claim

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: denial or payment recovery.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Below is a table of common modifiers, along with a brief description of how they are typically

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: applied for reimbursement and reporting. These guidelines are intended to address common

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: claim situations but may not apply in all cases, as modifier use can vary. For more detailed

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: information, refer to the CMS Medicare Claims Processing Manual Chapter 43 and Chapter 234,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: or the National Correct Coding Initiative (NCCI) guidelines.4

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: The purpose of this policy is to establish national drug code (NDC) billing requirements for all

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: continuous glucose monitor (CGM) claims. Providers must include accurate NDCs on all CGM

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: claims to ensure efficient processing and timely reimbursement. Missing NDCs can result in

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: claim denials or processing delays.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: This policy clarifies Devoted Health's classification of CGMs and their supplies, and diabetic

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: testing supplies, and outlines associated reimbursement requirements.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Continuous Glucose Monitors

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Per the Social Security Act §1861(s)(6), CGMs are covered under the DME benefit.1 In order for

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: a beneficiary's DME to be eligible for reimbursement, the reasonable and necessary

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: requirements specified in the related Local Coverage Determination (LCD)2 must be met as

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: well as additional payment policy requirements.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health covers specific CGM brands (FreeStyle Libre, Dexcom, and Guardian) for

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: eligible members. FreeStyle Libre devices do not require prior authorization; however,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Dexcom and Guardian require prior authorization to validate medical necessity. As of January

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: 1, 2026, Freestyle Libre Devices and Dexcom will not require prior authorization. Guardian,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Eversense, and other CGMs will require prior authorization.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Blood Glucometer and Diabetic Supplies

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health has preferred brands for blood glucometers and accompanying diabetic

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: testing supplies and applies preferred brand requirements to all diabetic supply claims.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Currently, both OneTouch and Accu-Chek are preferred brands. Effective January 1, 2026,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Accu-Chek will be the sole preferred brand. Beginning on this date, OneTouch and all other

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: non preferred brands will require an organization determination for coverage. Organization

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: determinations for non preferred brands will only be approved when there is a documented

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: medical reason the member cannot use the preferred brand.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: To ensure claims are can be accurately processed for payment, follow these billing guidelines:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: 1. Include the Required NDC

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Providers are required to include NDC information on claims for reimbursement of all

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: CGMs, CGM supplies, and diabetic testing supplies. The NDC must be an 11-digit

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: number in a 5-4-2 format. If the NDC has fewer than 11 digits, leading zeros must be

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: added. Examples are below; placeholders have been indicated with an asterisk:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: a. *XXXX-XXXX-XX = 0XXXX-XXXX-XX

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: b. XXXXX-*XXX-XX = XXXXX-0XXX-XX

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: c. XXXXX-XXXX-*X = XXXXX-XXXX-0X

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: NDCs should be submitted in the normalized 11-digit format, with no dashes or

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: spaces. Please preserve leading zeros. An example of the format is MMMMMDDDDPP :

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: 5-digit labeler, 4-digit product, 2-digit package.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: For a claim to be approved on the professional or facility submissions (CMS 1500/837P

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: or UB-04/837I), the following NDC information must be included:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● NDC number: A valid 11-digit NDC in the required format.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● Example NDC: 0591-0933-01 should be sent as 00591093301.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● Unit of Measure (UOM): Such as milliliters (ML), grams (GR), units (UN).

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● NDC quantity: The total quantity administered, including partial units (e.g., 1.5 ml).

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: For more information on NDCs, refer to our NDC Billing Guidelines payment policy.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: 2. Procedure Codes

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Use appropriate CPT codes (e.g., A4238, A4239, E2103, A4253, A4256, E0607, etc.) on

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: the CMS-1500, or X12 837P forms. Each claim line for these codes must include the

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: correct NDC.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: 1. Supply Allowance

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Bill CGM supplies under supply allowance CPT codes (A4238, or A4239), which cover

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: items such as sensors and transmitters. Supplies billed separately will be denied. Each

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: claim line billed under A4238 or A4239 must include the corresponding product NDC

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: for the specific sensor or transmitter supplied. Supplies billed without an NDC, or

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: supplies billed separately outside the allowance, may be denied.

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: Policy Overview

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: CMS designates certain hospitals as Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs) to improve healthcare access in

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: rural areas1. Services provided in CAHs are the same as those provided in a Prospective Payment

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: System (PPS) hospitals but are billed and paid under a different methodology2. This policy covers our

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: billing requirements for services provided at a CAH. specifically based on the methods defined by

extracted_content.title: Policy Overview
extracted_content.content: CMS for Method I and Method II billing.

extracted_content.title: SCOPE
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Critical Access Hospital (CAH): A hospital that participates in the State Medicare Rural Flexibility

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Program and meets the conditions of participation required by CMS.1

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Cost-to-Charge Ratio (CCR): The ratio between a hospital's billed charges and gross expenses.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Fiscal Intermediary Rate Letter (FIRL): A letter issued by CMS to a facility with their CCR percentage

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: and effective date.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Prospective Payment System (PPS): A payment methodology that pays predetermined, fixed

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: amounts based on average national costs that are adjusted based on geographic variances.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: WHAT WE COVER

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: We cover medically necessary services provided at a CAH. Under this policy, the same benefit limits

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: and prior authorization requirements for inpatient and outpatient services apply as those performed

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: in an acute care hospital. Covered services include:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Anesthesia services;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Facilities and related equipment (e.g., operating room);

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Laboratory Services;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Medical social services;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Medications and supplies used during the course of treatment;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Nursing and physician services;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Radiology and other diagnostic procedures;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Room and board or overnight observation.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: How to bill us

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: We reimburse claims according to Medicare payment rules. CAHs are exempt from PPS rules and are

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: instead paid on a reasonable cost basis calculated by the facility's CCR. For specific details regarding

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: the submission of your FIRLs, please refer to your contact.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Bill your inpatient claims on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) or X12 837I electronic equivalent, with bill type

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: 0111-0119. Be sure to include the appropriate revenue, HCPCS, and ICD-10-PCS codes.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Outpatient claims for CAHs can be submitted using one of the two CMS-approved billing methods, as

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: outlined below. Our billing follows the specific method chosen by the CAH, in line with CMS

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: regulations.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Method I (Standard): Separate Billing for Facility and Professional Charges3

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Facility and professional charges are submitted separately and follow industry coding standards:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Facility services are submitted on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) or an X12 837I transaction;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Use type of bill 085X and the appropriate frequency code (e.g., 0851, 0857).

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Facility claims will be reimbursed at the CCR.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Professional services are submitted on a CMS-1500 or X12 837P transaction;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Use place of service 19 or 22;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Professional claims will be reimbursed at the lesser of billed charges or 100% of the

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: locality-based facility rate of the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Method II (Optional): Combined Billing for Facility and Professional Charges4

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Facility and professional charges are submitted on the same claim and must use the following coding

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: standards:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ All services are submitted on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) or an X12 837I transaction;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Use type of bill 085X and the appropriate frequency code (e.g., 0851, 0857);

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Professional services are billed with the appropriate CPT/HCPCS code and one of the

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: following revenue codes: 096X, 097X, or 098X

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Facility charges will be paid at the CCR; while professional services are paid at 115% of the

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: locality-based facility rate of the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: For CAHs using Method I, this approach remains in place by default unless the CAH proactively opts

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: into Method II with CMS.5 Once a CAH selects Method II, CMS mandates that this choice remain

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: effective for all future cost reporting periods unless a written request to terminate the election is

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: submitted to CMS at least 30 days before the start of the next period.6 Consequently, our billing

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: practices are governed by CMS classifications, and any billing method preference changes must be

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: completed with CMS first.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Non-patient Laboratory Tests: CAHs may perform referred laboratory tests without directly

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: providing outpatient services to the member. These claims must be submitted on a CMS-1450

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: (UB-04) or an X12 837I transaction with type of bill 014X and the appropriate frequency code (e.g.,

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: 0141, 0147). Claims will be paid at the lesser of billed charges or 100% of the Clinical Laboratory Fee

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Schedule.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER

extracted_content.content: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Although treatment for a permanent crown may require multiple visits, a permanent crown is

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: considered a single covered service for reimbursement purposes.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: A permanent crown is complete only when it is cemented or bonded to the tooth (the seat date), and

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: reimbursement is based solely on that date.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Temporary crowns are not reimbursable, and all laboratory fees are included in the crown

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: reimbursement.

extracted_content.content: BILLING REQUIREMENTS

extracted_content.title: BILLING REQUIREMENTS
extracted_content.content: ● Providers must submit one claim representing the permanent crown treatment.

extracted_content.title: BILLING REQUIREMENTS
extracted_content.content: ● The claim must be submitted after the permanent crown is seated.

extracted_content.title: BILLING REQUIREMENTS
extracted_content.content: ● The date of service reported on the claim must be the seat (cementation) date.

extracted_content.title: INCOMPLETE TREATMENT
extracted_content.content: INCOMPLETE TREATMENT

extracted_content.title: INCOMPLETE TREATMENT
extracted_content.content: If the permanent crown is not seated (e.g., patient no-show, extraction of the tooth, or treatment

extracted_content.title: INCOMPLETE TREATMENT
extracted_content.content: discontinued), the permanent crown is considered incomplete and is not eligible for reimbursement.

extracted_content.content: This policy details the reimbursement standards for reporting unused or wasted drugs and

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: container), and multi-use containers (MDC). While providers are expected to schedule patients

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: efficiently to minimize drug waste, Devoted Health allows for payment of discarded amounts

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: Discarded Drug Guidelines

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: 1. Single-Dose Container (SDC)

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: If a portion of a SDC must be discarded after treating a patient, the program covers both the

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: administered and the discarded amounts.

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: ● Documentation: The patient's medical record must explicitly state the exact amount

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: given and the exact amount wasted.

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: ● Disposal: Wasted amounts must be discarded and cannot be used for any other

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: patient.

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: ● Container Selection: Claims must reflect the smallest available container size from

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: the manufacturer that satisfies the patient's dose. Billing for a larger container when a

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: smaller one was available is not permitted.

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: 2. Multi-Dose Container Vials (MDC)

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: ● No Reimbursement for Waste: Discarded amounts from MDC are not eligible for

extracted_content.title: Discarded Drug Guidelines
extracted_content.content: payment.

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: Billing and Modifiers

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: The JW Modifier (Drug Wastage)

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: ● Purpose: Used to report the amount of drug not administered.

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: ● Format: The administered amount is reported on one line; the wasted amount is

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: reported on a separate line with the JW modifier appended.

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: DEVOTED HEALTH FOR PUBLIC USE

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: Page 2 of 5

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: ● Threshold: The JW modifier is only used if the waste is equal to at least one full billing

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: unit.

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: ● Calculation: Round the administered amount up to the nearest unit and the discarded

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: amount down to the previous unit.

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: The JZ Modifier (No Wastage)

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: ● Purpose: Required for claims involving single-dose containers where zero drug was

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: discarded.

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: ● Format: The claim should include one line for the drug with the JZ modifier and the

extracted_content.title: Billing and Modifiers
extracted_content.content: total units administered.

extracted_content.title: Vial Rounding Guidelines
extracted_content.content: Vial Rounding Guidelines

extracted_content.title: Vial Rounding Guidelines
extracted_content.content: To promote clinical efficiency and minimize unnecessary drug waste, providers are

extracted_content.title: Vial Rounding Guidelines
extracted_content.content: encouraged to practice vial rounding when medically appropriate.

extracted_content.title: Vial Rounding Guidelines
extracted_content.content: ● Rounding Protocol: If a prescribed dose (e.g., 203 mg) slightly exceeds the total

extracted_content.title: Vial Rounding Guidelines
extracted_content.content: amount provided by full vials (e.g., two 100 mg vials), and the excess amount (3 mg)

extracted_content.title: Vial Rounding Guidelines
extracted_content.content: offers no additional therapeutic benefit, the provider should round the dose down to

extracted_content.title: Vial Rounding Guidelines
extracted_content.content: the nearest vial size (200 mg).

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: Key Restrictions & Reminders

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: ● Splitting Doses: It is prohibited to bill the full vial amount to multiple patients; bill

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: only for the units actually administered to each individual.

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: ● Missed Appointments: Wastage cannot be billed if the patient did not show up and no

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: drug was administered.

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: ● NOC Codes: "Not Otherwise Classified" codes should only be used if no specific HCPCS

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: code exists; a narrative description of the drug and dose must be included on the

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: claim.

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: ● Injection Fees: If an office visit is solely for an injection, payment is made only for the

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: injection service. Separate payment for injection services is not made if other

extracted_content.title: Key Restrictions & Reminders
extracted_content.content: physician fee schedule services are performed at the same time.

extracted_content.title: Documentation Guidelines
extracted_content.content: To ensure reimbursement, medical records must be legible and include:

extracted_content.title: Documentation Guidelines
extracted_content.content: ● Complete patient identification and date of service.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: As part of the claim adjudication process, we use Optum's Emergency Department Claim Analyzer

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: (EDC) to evaluate the level of the emergency room visit submitted. The goal of the EDC Analyzer is to

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: determine the appropriate facility level of service for emergency department visits based on a

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: consistent, objective, and automated methodology. The EDC Analyzer evaluates claim information to

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: identify the intensity of services provided during the emergency department visit and assigns a facility

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: level accordingly. This evaluation is not a medical necessity determination. Medical record review is not

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: performed and does not affect the outcome.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: For a more in-depth look at the Optum Emergency Department Claim Analyzer, refer to the Optum EDC

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Analyzer resources.

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: Proc".

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT
extracted_content.content: For example, if you submit a claim with CPT® 99285 and the relevant claim data only supports

extracted_content.title: POLICY STATEMENT

extracted_content.content: column.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Claims for eyewear provided following cataract surgery must include one of the diagnoses

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: listed below to ensure proper claims adjudication. The following diagnosis codes are required

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: to meet the benefit criteria for post-cataract eyewear:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● H27.00 Aphakia, unspecified eye

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● H27.01 Aphakia, right eye

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● H27.02 Aphakia, left eye

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● H27.03 Aphakia, bilateral

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Q12.3 Congenital aphakia

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Z96.1 Presence of intraocular lens

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Claims for post-cataract eyewear are subject to denial if the required diagnosis (DX) codes are

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: not present or do not accurately support the services billed.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: This policy documents our coverage and billing requirements for services provided by a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC). These are outpatient facilities that provide primary

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: and preventive health care services to medically underserved areas and populations that

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: would otherwise be provided in an outpatient clinic or physicianʼs office.1

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: When you see one of our members at your FQHC, we cover face-to-face encounters between

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: the patient and a Physician, Physician Assistant (PA), Nurse Practitioner (NP), Certified Nurse

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Midwife (CNM), Visiting Nurse, Clinical Psychologist (CP) or Clinical Social Worker (CSW)

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: during which a FQHC service is rendered.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: FQHCs can bill for a face-to-face, medically necessary visit furnished by a dentist, podiatrist,

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: optometrist, or chiropractor if the service furnished is on the list of qualifying visits for the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: FQHC and all other requirements are met. All services furnished must be within the state

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: scope of practice for the practitioner and all HCPCS codes must reflect the actual services that

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: were furnished.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: FQHC services include, but are not limited to:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: When multiple practitioners see our member on the same day, we generally consider it one

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: payable encounter. For example, if a member comes in to see an optometrist for an eye exam

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: and then sees their PCP for a wellness visit, it is still one payable encounter. However, If you

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: have discharged our member and they return on the same day for the diagnosis and/or

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: treatment of a new acute medical issue, we will consider this as a second payable encounter.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Mental health services provided on the same day as medical services are covered as a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: separate encounter but are subject to the same limitations. CMS requires that same-day

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: encounters be clearly distinct and medically justified in order to be paid separately (CMS

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Claims for FQHC services payable under the PPS need to be submitted on a CMS-1450

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: (UB-04) or X12 837I electronic equivalent with bill type 0771-0779 and include the

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: appropriate revenue, payment, and qualifying visit codes. Payment codes are reported on the

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: first line of the claim with a corresponding line that includes the CPT or HCPCS code that

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: represents the qualifying visit.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Preventive services provided on the same date of service as another qualifying visit are not

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: separately payable (unless addressed in the Vaccines section below), but a payment code

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: that represents both payment codes and visit codes must be reported to ensure our member

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: does not incur cost share. Separate and distinct medical encounters on the same date of

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: service require a payment and CPT code for each qualifying visit and include modifier 59 on

extracted_content.content: The purpose of this policy is to define guidelines for approximation pricing, also known as gap

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Approximation pricing, also referred to as gap fill pricing, is a reimbursement methodology

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: used to establish a payment rate for a medical service, procedure, or code when no defined

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: payment rate exists from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS).

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Under this approach, the payer determines an estimated allowable amount by evaluating

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: comparable services or rate sources, including factors such as:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Similar CPT/HCPCS codes

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Relative complexity and resource utilization

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Provider specialty and site of service

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Historical reimbursement patterns

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Regional market rates or benchmarks

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Gap fill pricing is commonly used for:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Newly established CPT/HCPCS codes

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Unlisted procedures

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Emerging technologies or services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Services without a CMS fee schedule amount

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: The resulting reimbursement amount is intended to approximate a reasonable payment until

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: an official CMS rate or contracted rate becomes available.

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: Providers must follow these CMS guidelines for accurate and timely claim submission. 3

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: ● 30-Day Episode : Each episode of care should be submitted as a single claim with a 30-day

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: ● Billing Visits : Each visit should be billed by date of service, with the correct revenue and

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: ○ Revenue Codes : Providers must include a valid HIPPS code and bill it with the 0023

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: revenue code to ensure accurate pricing. Claims missing a HIPPS code or submitted

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: without the 0023 revenue code may be denied or delayed in processing.

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements
extracted_content.content: ● Claim Format : Providers should submit claims via the 837i (CMS-1450/UB-04) for claims. If

extracted_content.title: Claim Submission Requirements

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: OVERVIEW

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: To uphold the highest standards of care for our members, we conduct claim and/or clinical reviews of

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: hospital admissions. These reviews assess the completeness, adequacy, and quality of hospital care

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: provided. Reviews are conducted in accordance with 42 CFR §476.71(a)(8)(ii) and other relevant CMS

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: guidelines.1, 2

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Scope

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Acronyms and definitions

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Initial Admission: An admission to the same or related hospital that is used to determine if a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: subsequent admission meets the criteria for a readmission.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Quality Improvement Organization (QIO): An entity contracted by CMS to perform case review and

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: quality improvement functions.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Same or Related Hospital: Any hospital system or hospital that is part of a hospital system that

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: shares the same contractual hospital agreement and/or tax identification number with any other

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: hospital or system.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Same-day Readmission: Defined as readmission occurring between midnight and midnight of a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: single day.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Policy statement

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: We may review readmission (re-hospitalization within a specified time interval) claims when a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: member returns to the same or related hospital within thirty (30) days of the discharge date of a prior

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admission. Consistent with CMS guidelines, we do not separately cover readmissions when they are

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: for a leave of absence, for the same or plausibly related condition as the prior stay, or considered

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: otherwise preventable.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: For the purposes of this policy, criteria for "same or plausibly related, or otherwise preventable"

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: include but are not limited to the following:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● The same or plausibly related procedure and/or diagnosis as the prior discharge;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Procedures and/or diagnoses related to infections or other complications of care;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Acute decompensation of a coexisting chronic condition;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Medical decision making inconsistent with professionally recognized standards of care;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Insufficient discharge planning and/or post-discharge follow up, such as lack of coordination

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: between inpatient and outpatient services;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Premature discharge resulting in readmission, such as signs of post-operative infection or

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: abnormal test results at the time of discharge.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Care that could have been provided during first admission (i.e., if the two confinements could

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: be related).

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Readmission was medically unnecessary.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Readmission was a result of circumvention of the Prospective Payment System.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: We will review claims and/or medical records for both admissions to determine if they are clinically

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: related and/or preventable. For additional guidance on readmission review criteria, please refer to

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: the Medicare QIO Case Review Manual and State Operations Manual.3, 4

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Exemptions from This Policy:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Readmissions that are unrelated to the prior discharge are covered as two separate admissions.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: We recognize that there are times when readmissions are required as part of regular treatment or

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: due to extenuating circumstances and are exempt from this policy. Examples include, but are not

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: limited to, the following:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Behavioral/mental health and substance abuse admissions;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Planned chemotherapy treatments;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Planned infusion treatments;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Neonatal or obstetrical admissions;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Transfers from Out-of-Network to In-Network facilities;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Transplant and transplant-related admissions.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Leave of Absence/Planned Readmission:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: If a patient is readmitted to a facility as part of a planned readmission or leave of absence, the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admissions are not considered two separate admissions. CMS requires the facility to submit one

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: claim and receive one combined MS-DRG payment for both admissions because both are for the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: treatment of the same episode of illness. Examples based on CMS guidelines include:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: "Hospitals may place a patient on a leave of absence when readmission is expected and the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: patient does not require a hospital level of care during the interim period. Examples could

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: include, but are not limited to, situations where surgery could not be scheduled immediately, a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: specific surgical team was not available, bilateral surgery was planned, or when further

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: treatment is indicated following diagnostic tests but cannot begin immediately."5

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Medical records for a leave of absence must clearly show that the readmission was planned and

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: related to the same episode of care. Leave of absence days are not covered by the plan and cannot be

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: charged to the member.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Same-day Readmission for Related Condition:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: If a patient is readmitted to a facility on the same day as a prior discharge for the same or a plausibly

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: related condition, CMS requires the facility to combine the two admissions on one claim. Consistent

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: with CMS billing requirements, Devoted Health, may review same-day readmissions and request

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: medical records to determine if the readmission was related. If a patient was readmitted during the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: same day for a same or plausibly related condition, Devoted Health will deny the subsequent

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admission. The provider must adjust the original admissions claim to combine both stays on the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: same claim to be eligible.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: If a patient leaves against medical advice (AMA) and then returns same-day to the same hospital, this

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: scenario will be considered a same-day readmission and should be billed as one claim.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Same-day Readmission for Unrelated Condition:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: If a patient is readmitted to a facility on the same day as a prior discharge for symptoms unrelated to

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: the prior stay's medical condition, CMS requires the facility to follow different billing requirements. In

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: this situation, two claims are submitted, but the claim for the subsequent admission must contain

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: the condition code "B4". Consistent with CMS billing requirements, if a patient is readmitted on the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: same day for an unrelated condition, two properly coded claims must be submitted to Devoted

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Health.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Transfer:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: A discharge of a hospital inpatient is considered to be a transfer if the patient is admitted on the same

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: day to another hospital. A transfer between acute inpatient hospitals occurs when a patient is

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admitted to a hospital and is subsequently transferred from the hospital where the patient was

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: admitted to another hospital for additional treatment once the patient's condition has stabilized or a

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: diagnosis established.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Effective for discharges on or after October 1, 2003, patients who leave AMA but are admitted to

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: another inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) hospital on the same day as they left will be

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: treated as transfers, and the transfer payment policy will apply.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Claim submission and reimbursement

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: We process claims according to Medicare PPS payment rules unless otherwise specified by your

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: contract. Claims for readmissions that are billed separately but are not separately payable will be

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: denied and may be submitted as outlined below:

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Readmission for the Same or Related Condition Within Thirty (30) Days

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Submit a corrected claim (TOB 117) that references the original claim number;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Consolidate both admissions into one claim.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Planned Readmission/Leave of Absence

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Submit all admissions related to the episode of care on one claim;

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Report leave of absence date span with Occurrence Span Code 74 (FL 35-36);

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Report non-covered charges using revenue code 018X in FL 42.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ● Same-Day Readmissions for Unrelated Conditions

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: ○ Same-day readmissions for conditions unrelated to the prior discharge are reimbursed

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: as two separate MS-DRG payments. Billing should follow standard IPPS requirements

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: and include condition code B4 in FL 18-28.

extracted_content.title: 1. Routine Services

extracted_content.title: 1. Routine Services

extracted_content.title: 1. Routine Services
