extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines our requirements for National Drug Code (NDC) information to ensure

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: that providers follow proper procedures for submitting claims by including the required

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: National Drug Code (NDC) information. NDCs serve as standardized identifiers for

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: medications, capturing key details such as the manufacturer, drug name, and dosage. To

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: qualify for reimbursement, claims must include a valid NDC number, the NDC unit of measure,

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: and the total NDC quantity dispensed on all drug claim lines. The policy reinforces adherence

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: to industry best practices for claims processing, helping prevent billing errors and delays.

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health Plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Providers are required to include NDC information on all drug claim lines for reimbursement.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Drug claim lines billed without the complete NDC information (valid NDC number, NDC UOM,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: and quantity) may be subject to denial, including denial of all associated lines.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: NDCs are 11-digit numbers that identify the drug manufacturer, name, dosage, strength,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: package size, and quantity. The number is composed of three segments, denoted in a 5-4-2

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: format and can typically be found on the product's label or packaging. For multi-unit

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: packaging, such as a box with several vials, the NDC from the outer packaging should be used.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: If the NDC on the packaging has fewer than 11 digits, leading zeros are required.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Examples are outlined below; placeholders have been indicated with an asterisk.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Examples:

extracted_content.content: For a claim to be approved on the professional or facility submissions (CMS 1500/837P or

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● NDC number: A valid 11-digit NDC in the required format.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Example NDC: 0591-0933-01 should be sent as 00591093301.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Unit of Measure (UOM): Such as milliliters (ML), grams (GR), units (UN).

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● NDC quantity: The total quantity administered, including partial units (e.g., 1.5 ml).

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Examples of Scenarios Requiring NDCs:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: NDCs are required for all drug claim lines. Examples include but are not limited to:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● When members supply their own product or medication, the provider must include the NDC

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: (or itemize the product through a $0 or penny charge).

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● When administering or dispensing a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) device or

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: diabetic supplies.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● When multiple drugs or doses are given.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Reimbursement Clarification:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: If NDC is missing, incorrect, incomplete, or incompatible with the HCPCS or CPT code(s)

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: submitted, the associated drug line or claim may be subject to denial. Resubmit the corrected

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: claim with accurate NDC information and the claim will be reconsidered for reimbursement.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: The quantity of medication billed should not exceed the maximum units allowed by the NDC

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: or packaging limits. Claims that exceed these limits or are not aligned with packaging

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: increments will be denied.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Providers are also required to use appropriate modifiers, such as JW (wastage) and JZ (zero

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: wastage), for single-use vials to comply with CMS regulations.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: OVERVIEW

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: This policy establishes that Devoted Health will reimburse SNF providers only through the date

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: coverage would appropriately end under a valid Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage (NOMNC).

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Pursuant to CMS § 260.5.6, when a provider fails to submit the clinical documentation required by

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: the BFCC-QIO during a member appeal and coverage continues as a result, the provider may be held

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: financially liable.1 In these cases, Devoted Health will limit payment to the valid NOMNC effective

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: date. Under CMS § 260.3.6 when a NOMNC is invalid or not delivered, the provider remains financially

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: liable until a valid notice is issued and the required CMS timeframe has passed.2 Any SNF days billed

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: after the valid NOMNC effective date or CMS-defined liability cutoff (when it is determined a valid

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: NOMNC was not issued) will be denied as provider liable.

extracted_content.title: SCOPE
extracted_content.content: SCOPE

extracted_content.title: SCOPE
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plan members and all participating Skilled Nursing Facility

extracted_content.title: SCOPE
extracted_content.content: SNF providers.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: NOMNC: Notice of Medicare Non-Coverage. A standardized CMS-required notice that informs a

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Medicare beneficiary when coverage for a service is ending.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: BFCC-QIO: Beneficiary and Family-Centered Care Quality Improvement Organization. The

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: independent review entity responsible for conducting expedited determination requests under the

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: NOMNC process.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health will reimburse SNF services only through the effective date listed on a valid NOMNC.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: When coverage continues because the provider did not meet its obligations under the expedited

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: determination process, or when a NOMNC is found invalid or undelivered, the resulting days of

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: service are the financial responsibility of the provider. SNF days billed after the applicable NOMNC

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: effective date, or after the date coverage would have appropriately ended had a valid notice been

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: issued, will be denied as provider liable.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Member Wins the Appeal Due to Provider Failure to Submit Required Documentation

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: When a provider does not submit the BFCC-QIO with the medical records or information necessary to

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: complete an expedited review, the BFCC-QIO may render a favorable decision for the member based

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: solely on the information available.1 CMS requires providers to submit all requested medical records

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: by close of business on the day of BFCC-QIO notification.3 Failure to meet these requirements

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: prevents the BFCC-QIO from determining medical necessity.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: In such cases, Devoted Health will limit payment to the effective date on the valid NOMNC issued by

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the facility. All SNF days beyond that date are the financial responsibility of the provider, and any

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: such days billed will be denied as provider liable.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Provider Failure to Issue a Valid NOMNC

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: CMS requires that the NOMNC be delivered at least two calendar days before coverage ends and

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: include all required elements.4 If the BFCC-QIO determines that a NOMNC is invalid or was not

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: delivered, the facility is financially liable for all days of service beyond the date coverage would have

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: appropriately ended under a valid notice.2 Devoted Health will not reimburse SNF services furnished

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: beyond the date coverage would have appropriately ended under a valid notice. When a NOMNC is

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: invalid or not delivered, the provider remains liable for continued services until a new valid notice is

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: issued and either:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● two calendar days have passed after the beneficiary receives the valid notice, or

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● the effective date listed on the new notice occurs,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: whichever is later.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Subsequent Medical-Necessity Appeal Outcomes

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: If a member initially wins an expedited appeal on a technical basis (including, but not limited to, a

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: facility's failure to submit required documentation to the BFCC-QIO or the issuance of an invalid

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: NOMNC), the facility is financially liable for continued services as defined under CMS rules, including

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: However, if the facility subsequently issues a valid NOMNC and the member prevails on a later

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: BFCC-QIO appeal on medical-necessity grounds, the plan will backdate coverage to include all days

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the BFCC-QIO determines to be medically necessary. This includes days that were provider-liable

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: solely due to the earlier technical defect. Only days determined not medically necessary, or days

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: following the end of the medically necessary period, will remain provider-liable.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Observation care is furnished to provide short-term treatment and monitoring to assess the severity

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: of emergent cases and determine if a member can be treated and discharged or admitted to the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: hospital for an inpatient stay. This policy documents our coverage and billing requirements for these

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: services.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Ambulatory Payment Classification (APC): a classification code assigned to a group of clinically

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: similar services and hospital resources for the purpose of payment. Payment is considered inclusive

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: for all services assigned to an APC. For a full list of APC grouping and HCPCS assignments, please

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: refer to addendum A and B of the OPPS Calendar Year Notice of Final Rulemaking.1

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS): a payment methodology that pays

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: predetermined, fixed amounts based on average national costs that are adjusted based on

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: geographic variances.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Payment Status Indicator: a code assigned to each HCPCS code that identifies whether a service is

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: considered separately payable or packaged. For a full list and description of status indicators, please

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: WHAT WE COVER

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: When our member is placed in observation status, we will cover all medically necessary services for

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: stays up to 96 hours. We don't require that you notify us of an observation status but we strongly

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: recommend it.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: CMS guidelines note:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: "In the majority of cases, the decision whether to discharge a patient from the hospital following

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: resolution of the reason for the observation care or to admit the patient as an inpatient can be made

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: in less than 48 hours, usually in less than 24 hours. In only rare and exceptional cases do reasonable

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: and necessary outpatient observation services span more than 48 hours."3

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Stays over 96 hours are subject to clinical review prior to payment and may be denied for lack of

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: medical necessity.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Submit your claims on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) or X12 837I electronic equivalent with the one of the

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: following bill types and claim elements:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● Revenue code 0760 or 0762; and

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● HCPCS G0378.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: We will process a claim as observation when:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● Observation is billed in conjunction with one of these services:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ○ Outpatient hospital clinic visit (G0463);

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ○ Emergency department visit (type A and B) (99281-99285; G0380-G0384);

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ○ Critical Care (99291);

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ○ Direct referral to a hospital for observation by a provider in a community setting,

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: unrelated to any of the above services (G0379)

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● Observation hours are equal to or greater than 8, and

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● There are no services reported on the claim with a Status Indicator of "T" or "J1".

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: We process claims according to Medicare OPPS payment rules, including the use of Ambulatory

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Payment Classification (APC) groupings, Payment Status Indicators (SI), and the packaging of

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: services. Please refer to your contract for specific details.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Reimbursement for claims with observation hours that don't meet the criteria in this policy will be

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: packaged with the payment(s) for the service(s) with the highest APC classification assigned. All

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: outpatient hospital services provided on the same date as the observation period must be submitted

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: on the same claim for accurate adjudication.

extracted_content.content: If there is no prior authorization on file, claims with more than 96 units of G0378 will be denied.

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: PURPOSE

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: In 2019, CMS finalized a site-neutral policy reducing the payment rate for services rendered by

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: off-campus provider-based hospital departments (PBD). The payment rate was reduced to 40% of the

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS), codified at 42 CFR § 419.48(a).1 This reduction

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: applies to both excepted PBDs (billing with modifier PO) and non-excepted PBDs (billing with

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: modifier PN). For non-excepted off-campus PBDs, CMS applied a 60% reduction, reimbursing services

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: at approximately 40% of the OPPS rate, aligning with the Physician Fee Schedule (PFS) rates. . This

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: phased-in reduction began in CY2019 with a 30% reduction in payments and was fully implemented

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: in CY20202. This policy documents how we process claims for services provided in these locations,

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: including application of the PO and PN modifiers and corresponding payment reductions, and

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: outlines the outcomes of claims submitted without appropriate modifiers.3

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Consistent with CMS regulations and 42 CFR § 419.48(a)1 , we require modifier PO and/or PN to be

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: reported on claims for services rendered in an off-campus provider-based department, as defined in

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: this policy:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Modifier PO must be reported on claims submitted by all excepted off-campus PBDs.6

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Modifier PN must be reported on claims submitted by all non-excepted off-campus PBDs.6

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: This policy does not apply to:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Critical Access Hospitals (CAHs).

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Any facility that does not meet the definition of provider-based under 42 CFR § 413.65.4

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: When Devoted Health receives professional claims billed with place of service code 19 and the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: associated facility claim is billed without one of the appropriate service setting modifiers, Devoted

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: will use claim history to determine the appropriate payment methodology. If Devoted determines

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: that the claim should have been submitted with either modifier PO or PN, we will apply the payment

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: reduction. Payments are subject to retrospective review to ensure accuracy and claims that were not

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: billed accordingly are subject to adjustment.

extracted_content.content: Page 2 of 5

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Claim Submission and Reimbursement

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health processes claims according to Medicare OPPS and PFS payment rules, unless

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: otherwise specified by your contract. This includes, but is not limited to, Ambulatory Payment

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Classification (APC) grouping, Payment Status Indicators (SI), and Packaging of services.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Modifier PO must be reported when billing hospital outpatient services that are performed in an

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: excepted off-campus provider-based department of a hospital under the OPPS.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Modifier PN must be reported on every claim line for non-excepted items and services furnished by

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: an off-campus, outpatient, provider-based department of a hospital.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Add PO or PN modifier(s) to each HCPCS line item on the UB-04 claim when the service is:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Provided in an off-campus hospital outpatient department

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● The department is provider-based to the hospital

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● The department is "excepted" under Section 603

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● The service is billed under OPPS

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Services furnished in an emergency department are exempt from these billing requirements.6

extracted_content.content: ● Excepted Department: A department of a main provider that meets the statutory criteria

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ● Provider-based Department (PBD): A department or clinic that is under the same name and

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ownership of the main provider, including financial and administrative management.4

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: payment reductions.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ● PO Modifier: Identifies services furnished in excepted off-campus PBDs, subject to payment

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: reductions.

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: This policy explains our coverage and reimbursement requirements for Medicare-covered organ

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: transplants.

extracted_content.title: SCOPE
extracted_content.content: SCOPE

extracted_content.title: SCOPE
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all of our plans.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Diagnosis-Related Group (DRG) - A classification system that determines Medicare payment for

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: inpatient hospital stays based on diagnosis, treatment, and other factors.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Organ Acquisition Cost (OAC) - The reasonable costs incurred by a hospital for procuring organs for

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: transplant, reimbursed separately by Medicare.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: Prospective Payment System (PPS) - A Medicare reimbursement method that pays a fixed,

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: pre-determined amount for healthcare services.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: WHAT WE COVER

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: We cover Medicare-covered organ and stem cell transplants and their acquisition costs1 for our

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: members when medical necessity criteria are met and prior authorization has been obtained.2

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Covered transplants include:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Intestines;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Heart;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Kidneys;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Liver;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Lungs;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Pancreas;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Stem cells.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: In accordance with CMS guidelines, we do not cover kidney acquisition costs and those must be

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: billed directly to Medicare.1 Pre-transplant services for donors are not separately covered and are

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: considered part of the kidney acquisition cost.3

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: Submit your transplant claims on a CMS-1450 (UB-04) with bill type 011X and the appropriate

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: frequency code. Organ acquisition charges must be included on the same claim as the surgical

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: procedure and be reported with one of the following revenue codes:

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: ● 0810 or 0812 for solid organs;

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: 0815 for harvesting of stem cells.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: The base DRG payment will be calculated according to Medicare IPPS payment rules. Covered PPS

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: charges are calculated using the total charge amount on the claim, less the billed charges on the

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: organ acquisition claim lines or the facility-specific standard organ acquisition cost, whichever is

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: greater. Please see your contract for specific details.

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: To determine the payment amount for organ acquisition costs, we will need your most recent D4 or

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: D6 worksheet. We calculate the OAC by dividing the number of usable Medicare organs by the total

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: net cost reported in Part III: Summary of Costs and Charges (lines 63 and 69). If we do not receive the

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: necessary worksheets after 30 calendar days from the date you were notified, the claim will be paid

extracted_content.title: HOW TO BILL YOUR CLAIMS
extracted_content.content: and acquisition costs will be considered inclusive to the DRG payment.

level, fails to identify a definitive, non-primary clinical specialty
or specific area of practice for the purpose of benefit
determination. 
This includes Level II generic classifications (e.g.,
363L00000X-Nurse Practitioner, or 363A00000X-Physician
Assistant, as well as broad Level III specifications (e.g.,

The plan benefit tier - Primary Care or Specialty - that governs
the member cost-sharing applied to a given claim, as defined in
the applicable Evidence of Coverage (EOC).

Any claim-level or provider-level data element that affirmatively
indicates the rendering provider was functioning in a primary
care capacity at the time of service. See Section 5 for qualifying
signals.

363LP0808X - Psychiatric-Mental Health NP).

signals.

extracted_content.content: In accordance with the Affordable Care Act (ACA), the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Provider Terminations and the

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Q6 Modifier

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: DEVOTED HEALTH FOR PUBLIC USE

extracted_content.title: OVERVIEW
extracted_content.content: Page 1 of 4

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: PURPOSE

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines requirements for appropriate billing using the Q6 modifier when a provider

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: terminates from a practice. It ensures compliance with Medicare rules regarding substitute physician

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: arrangements under locum tenens billing when a provider has departed, and clarifies how claims must

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: be submitted during the allowable 60-day post-termination period.

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health Plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: When a provider terminates from a group practice, the practice must submit the provider's

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: true and actual departure date for system termination. Practices may not defer the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: submission of a determination date to extend billing privileges using the Q6 modifier

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Following a provider's termination, substitute physicians may continue to render services,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: and the group may bill under the terminated provider's NPI with the Q6 modifier appended to

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the claim, under a fee-for-time compensation arrangement, 3. This is permissible for a

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: maximum of sixty (60) continuous calendar days from the effective termination date3. The

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: window begins on the provider's termination date, not on the first date of Q6 billing. Claims

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: utilizing the Q6 modifier beyond the 60-day period will be adjudicated according to standard

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: processing rules.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: How to bill your claims

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: When billing for services rendered after a provider's termination, the following requirements

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: must be met to ensure compliant claim submission:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: For services performed prior to a provider's termination date, groups should continue to bill

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: using the provider's NPI without any modifiers, as usual. No Q6 modifier is needed if the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: regular provider personally rendered the services. For services rendered after a provider's

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: termination where a substitute physician was utilized, the group must bill under the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: terminated provider's NPI and append the Q6 modifier at the line level2, 3. The modifier signals

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: that a locum tenens arrangement is in place and that billing is occurring under the fee-for-time

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: compensation rules allowed by CMS.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: DEVOTED HEALTH FOR PUBLIC USE

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Page 2 of 4

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: When submitting these claims:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● The claim must reflect the terminated provider's NPI as the rendering provider.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● The procedure code(s) must be accompanied by the Q6 modifier.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Documentation supporting the use of the substitute physician must be maintained by

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the group in the event of audit or claims review3.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Date of service for these claims must be within the 60-calendar-day window following

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the provider's effective termination date.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ● Locum Tenens: A substitute physician temporarily providing services for a regular

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: provider.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ● Q6 Modifier: Billing modifier indicating services performed by a locum tenens

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: physician under fee-for-time arrangement.

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: ● 60-Day Window: The continuous period allowed for billing under the Q6 modifier

extracted_content.title: ACRONYMS AND DEFINITIONS
extracted_content.content: following provider absence or termination.

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: PURPOSE

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: This policy explains how we cover and pay for radiopharmaceuticals.

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted covers radiopharmaceuticals that are covered under Part B of original Medicare.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Please bill your claims on a CMS-1500 or X12 837P electronic equivalent.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Each MAC determines the reimbursement methodology for radiopharmaceuticals billed on

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: claims within its jurisdiction. The reimbursement guidelines can vary by MAC and by

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: procedure code. Please refer to the relevant MAC for its specific reimbursement

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: methodologies.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Unless there is an exception in a provider's contract, Devoted reimburses for

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: radiopharmaceutical procedure codes according to the guidelines set forth by each MAC,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: specifically:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● When there is a Medicare allowed amount for a procedure code, Devoted will pay

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: based on the rate provided by the MAC; and

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● When reimbursement for a procedure code is based on the invoice cost, Devoted will

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: pay based on the invoice information provided with the claim.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: When submitting invoice information on the claim, please follow these requirements;

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: otherwise, your claim may be denied. For how to bill a specific procedure code, please see

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the MAC guidelines:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Specify the total number of units provided to the member under the "unit of service"

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: field on the claim in box 24G on CMS-1500 or its electronic equivalent of Loop 2400,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: SV104 as follows:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: DEVOTED HEALTH FOR PUBLIC USE

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Page 2 of 5

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● When a procedure code descriptor includes "per study dose" and a range of

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: millicuries, please bill one unit of service per study.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: "Example 1: HCPCS code A9503 is defined as Technetium Tc-99m, medronate,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: diagnostic, per study dose, up to 30 millicuries. If the provider administers one

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: to 30 millicuries of this radiopharmaceutical agent for a study, code A9503

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: should be billed as one unit of service."3

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● When a procedure code description includes per millicurie (mCi) or 1 mCi,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: please bill per millicurie. The number of millicurie given to the patient should

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: be listed as the number of units.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: "Example 2: HCPCS code A9512 is defined as Technetium Tc-99m pertechnetate,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: diagnostic, per mCi. If the provider administers 5 mCi of this

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: radiopharmaceutical agent for a study, then the number of units would be listed

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: as 5 on the claim.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Example 3: HCPCS code A9595 is defined as Piflufolastat f-18, diagnostic, 1 mCi. If

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the provider administers 9 mCi of this radiopharmaceutical agent for a study,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: then the number of units would be listed as 9 on the claim." 3

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Include clear cost information as follows either in box 19 of CMS-1500 or its electronic

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: equivalent of Loop 2300 Segment NTE (header level) or Loop 2400 Segment NTE (line

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: level)

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ If the amount of the invoice is equal to the amount that is applicable to the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: patient and service on the claim, please enter this amount including cents e.g.,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ If the amount of the invoice is different from the amount that is applicable to

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the patient and service on the claim, please enter the following information:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ■ DES = Description/Name of agent

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ■ QS = Quantity shipped

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ■ TA = Total amount charged for quantity shipped in dollars and cents with

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the decimal

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ■ UP = Unit Price in dollars and cents with the decimal (optional)

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: DEVOTED HEALTH FOR PUBLIC USE

extracted_content.content: Page 3 of 5

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ■ DG = Dosage given

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: This information should be reported on one line as shown in the following

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: example:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: DES = TC-99m MDP QS = 100mci TA = $57.40 UP = $0.57 per mci DG = 25mci4

extracted_content.content: When our member is seen by multiple practitioners on the same day, we generally consider it

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: services are covered as a separate encounter but are subject to the same limitations.

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: PURPOSE

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: Clinical criteria for the identification and treatment of sepsis were established in 1991, but

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: have been revised over time to reflect the significant advances in the understanding of the

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: biopathology and management of the disease. The first revision in 2001, known as Sepsis-2,

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: was the prevailing standard until Sepsis-3 was defined in 2016. This policy states our adoption

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: of Sepsis-3 as the clinical criteria to be used when considering the medical necessity of

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: sepsis-related treatment.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: WHAT WE COVER

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: We cover medically necessary inpatient services for the treatment of sepsis, which is defined

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: as "a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection"

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: and septic shock as "a subset of sepsis in which underlying circulatory and cellular/metabolic

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: abnormalities are profound enough to substantially increase mortality."4

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: We will consider services medically necessary when our member's medical record indicates

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: the following:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Suspected or documented infection, and

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● A qSOFA score of 2 or more:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ GCS less than 14, or more than 1 point less than baseline.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Systolic blood pressure less than or equal to 100 mmHg;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ○ Respiratory rate greater than or equal to 22 BPM.

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: OR

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Suspected or documented infection, and

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● An acute increase of 2 or more SOFA points (baseline can be assumed to be 0 when

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: there is no known pre-existing organ dysfunction).

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: We will consider the services billed for septic shock medically necessary when our member's

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: medical record indicates the following:

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Diagnosis of sepsis;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: DEVOTED HEALTH FOR PUBLIC USE

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Page 2 of 5

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Persisting hypotension requiring vasopressors to maintain a MAP greater than or equal

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: to 65 mmhg;

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: ● Persistent lactic acidemia (serum lactate level greater than 2 mmol/L).

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: Authorization is required for all inpatient admissions. You must notify us about emergent

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: admissions within one business day of the admission date for concurrent review and care

extracted_content.title: WHAT WE COVER
extracted_content.content: planning.

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: PURPOSE

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: The purpose of this policy is to ensure access to high-quality care for Devoted Health

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: members through the provision of telehealth services. It establishes the framework for

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: reimbursement of telehealth services, including telephone services, virtual check-ins, and

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: e-visits. Telehealth services are defined as healthcare delivered remotely via

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: telecommunications technologies, and occur when the healthcare provider and the patient

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: are in separate locations, employing technology to bridge healthcare delivery.

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to all Devoted Health Plans.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Outlined below are the telehealth services covered under this policy, including, but not

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: limited to, specific codes, place of service (POS) designations, and common modifiers. For the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: purposes of this policy, telehealth encompasses synchronous and asynchronous

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: communication between providers and our members. This includes live, interactive audio or

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: audio-visual sessions, and asynchronous exchanges.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Providers must ensure that claims clearly indicate when services are delivered via telehealth.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Whether identified through place of service (POS) codes, telehealth modifiers, or other

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: documentation, we will process claims as long as telehealth delivery is evident.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Additionally, providers must meet all CMS requirements for rendering telehealth services,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: including licensure, scope of practice, and professional standards in the state(s) of both the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: practitioner and patient.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Note on Telehealth Waivers

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health has been applying Congressionally-authorized telehealth coverage waivers,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: which are set to expire on September 30, 2025. Effective October 1, 2025, claims for telehealth

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: services will be subject to applicable CMS limitations unless the services qualify under an

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: additional telehealth services benefit. For further details on these limitations, refer to CMS

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: guidance provided in the References section of this policy.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Additional Telehealth Services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Telehealth services covered under an additional telehealth benefit in the member's

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: applicable Evidence of Coverage (EOC) are eligible for reimbursement. Unless restricted by

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: federal statute or regulation, Devoted Health will allow additional telehealth services if the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: following conditions are met:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● The service is clinically appropriate for delivery via telecommunications-based

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: technology.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● The service is covered under the plan's benefit structure.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● All applicable coding and billing requirements are satisfied.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Other Virtual Services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health also covers other virtual services that are reimbursable under Original

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Medicare but are not classified as telehealth services, including:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● E-visits

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Virtual check-ins

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Remote monitoring

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Below is a detailed breakdown to clarify the scope of reimbursement and compliance

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: requirements.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Telehealth Services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Coverage includes original Medicare telehealth services, as well as other virtual services, such

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: as telephone services, e-visits, and virtual check-ins. Telehealth services must meet CMS

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: guidelines, including applicable CPT/HCPCS codes and modifiers. Services may include

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: synchronous audio-visual sessions, asynchronous exchanges, and audio-only services where

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: applicable.

extracted_content.content: Additional Covered Services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: In addition to the Medicare-covered and additional telehealth services, the following services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: are covered under this policy. These services may be provided via telehealth and are intended

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: to support the care and management of patients with various healthcare needs. The list

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: below includes, but is not limited to, the following services:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Annual Wellness Visits HCPCS codes G0438 and G0439.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Behavioral health integration and advanced care planning.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Chronic Care Management (CCM) and Transitional Care Management (TCM) Services:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: CPT codes 99495 and 99496.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ End-stage renal disease (ESRD) and nutrition therapy services.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Psychiatric Services CPT 90791, 90792, and psychiatric codes 90832-90838.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Remote Physiologic Monitoring: CPT codes 99453-99458.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Remote Therapeutic Monitoring: CPT 98975 and CPT 98980

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Modifiers

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: The following modifiers should be used when submitting claims for telehealth services to

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: indicate the type of telehealth service provided and the mode of communication used.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Properly using these modifiers ensures accurate billing and compliance with payer

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: requirements for telehealth services.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Modifier 93: Audio-only telehealth services (not required for 98000 - 98015 series).2

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Modifier 95: Audio-visual telehealth services (not required for 98000 - 98015 series).3

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.content: ○ Modifier GQ: Telehealth service rendered via an asynchronous telecommunications

extracted_content.content: system.3

extracted_content.content: CPT Code Updates

extracted_content.content: Please note, the following updates to the CPT code set will apply to telehealth claims. These

extracted_content.content: ○ Removals: Codes 99441-99443 will be retired, and no longer accepted on claims.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Claims submitted with these codes will be denied for payment or subject to delays.

extracted_content.content: The purpose of this policy is to establish a compliant operational standard for the application

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: of the KX modifier on outpatient therapy claims. This policy ensures that all physical therapy

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: (PT), occupational therapy (OT), and speech-language pathology (SLP) services exceeding

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: Medicare annual financial thresholds strictly adhere to federal medical necessity

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: In accordance with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) guidelines and the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Bipartisan Budget Act of 2018, this organization requires providers to append the KX modifier

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: to therapy claims once a patientʼs annual incurred expenses reach the designated threshold.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: For Calendar Year (CY) 2026, the statutory financial threshold is established at $2,480 (applied

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: to PT/SLP combined, and a separate $2,480 for OT).

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: The application of the KX modifier on a claim form serves as a binding, formal attestation by

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the clinician and the organization that:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: The continued services are reasonable and medically necessary.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: The patient requires the skills of a licensed therapist to achieve safe, effective

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: outcomes.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: The clinical documentation directly supports the need for extended treatment.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health reserves the right to conduct periodic, retrospective, or concurrent audits of

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: provider medical records. The purpose of these audits is to verify that documentation fully

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: supports the utilization of the KX modifier and justifies the medical necessity of services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: rendered past the threshold. Providers are required to furnish complete records upon request

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: within the timeframe specified in request for medical records letter.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Do not append Modifier KX to therapy claims that have not exceeded the financial threshold

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: limit.

extracted_content.content: This policy outlines how Devoted Health administers and reimburses services deemed

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: unrelated to the terminal condition for members enrolled in hospice care.

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: This policy applies to members with an active hospice election through CMS at the time

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY
extracted_content.content: services are rendered, regardless of provider type or place of service.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: 1. Medicare Advantage organizations are responsible for ensuring that members with an

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: active hospice election through CMS have access to all Medicare-covered services that

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: are unrelated to the terminal condition, as well as any non-hospice services not

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: covered by Medicare but included as supplemental benefits under the plan.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: 2. Services furnished to a member who has elected hospice that are not related to the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: terminal illness are considered non-hospice services. For example, services rendered

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: by an attending physician who is not employed by or under contract with the

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: member's hospice provider are classified as non-hospice services and may be

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: reimbursed under Original Medicare.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: 3. Because a Medicare Advantage organization cannot submit claims to an A/B MAC (A),

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: and an A/B MAC (A) cannot issue payment to a Medicare Advantage organization,

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Devoted Health will administer billing for non-hospice ("other") services furnished by

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: providers in accordance with the following approach.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: a. Devoted Health requires providers or suppliers (e.g., hospitals or physicians) to

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: bill the Medicare Administrative Contractor (MAC) directly for non-hospice

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ("other") services. In such cases, providers should submit claims to the MAC as

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: the primary payer. Following adjudication, providers must then submit a

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: secondary claim to Devoted Health, including the Explanation of Payment

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: (EOP), for consideration of any additional reimbursement.

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: This policy outlines how Devoted Health covers and reimburses vision-related services,

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: including both Medicare-covered ophthalmologic services and supplemental routine vision

extracted_content.title: PURPOSE
extracted_content.content: benefits available to our members. It details the types of services covered, applicable

extracted_content.title: APPLICABILITY

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: We cover all Medicare-covered vision services, in addition to supplemental benefits not

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: available through Medicare. This includes:

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Medicare-Covered

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Diabetic retinopathy screenings;

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Glaucoma screenings;

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Surgical eye procedures;

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Specialist and/or physician services

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ● Supplemental

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Routine eye exams;

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Routine or minor eye procedures;

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: ○ Routine vision hardware

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Screening and routine eye exams are covered once every year at no cost to our members.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Members must have a diagnosis of diabetes to be eligible for retinopathy screenings.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Routine prescription vision hardware is covered with an annual allowance that can be applied

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: toward frames, lenses, contacts (excluding contact lens fittings), repairs, and other related

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: costs. Please see the "Vision Care" section of our EOC for plan specific allowances listed under

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: "Eyewear," as the allowance amount and how members access their benefit may vary

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: depending on the member's plan.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Post-cataract eyewear is a Medicare covered service and is a separate benefit from members'

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: annual routine eyewear allowance.

extracted_content.content: DEVOTED HEALTH FOR PUBLIC USE

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Please note: Annual benefit limitations are applied based on the calendar year (1/1 - 12/31)

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: and are not based on time passed since the last date of service.

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: Minor and surgical procedures are covered as medically necessary and may be subject to prior

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: authorization. Cost-shares may vary based on our member's plan and site of service, but will

extracted_content.title: POLICY

extracted_content.title: POLICY
extracted_content.content: at an Outpatient Hospital."
